verdict.rationale: Braintrust says evals can 'Score outputs with LLMs, code, or humans', and scorers that produce numeric scores are a first-class object. Scorers can be iterated in no-code playgrounds, authored via MCP, and managed through the API, and they can run in experiments or as online scoring on production traces. That covers the core of configurable LLM-based scoring. missing for 10: detailed documentation of LLM-as-a-judge configuration (judge prompt, model choice, scoring rubric/choice mapping), concrete LLM-judge code examples (the GitHub sample uses LevenshteinScorer), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can score outputs with configurable LLM-as-a-judge evaluators

citations.quote: Measure quality with evals — Score outputs with LLMs, code, or humans
Scorers measure quality with numeric scores, while classifiers assign labels so you can group and analyze results
Playgrounds provide a no-code workspace for rapidly iterating on prompts, models, scorers, and datasets.
Query production logs, author prompts and scorers, configure monitoring, and run evals
Online scoring evaluates production traces automatically as they’re logged, running asynchronously with no impact on latency.
